title: GSC engine field catalogue
description: One game's script-visible engine fields (the fields the engine registers on each object kind: entity, player, actor, vehicle, hud element, path node, weapon ...), as extracted from the game's executable. Validates fields/<engine-id>.toml after TOML parsing. Facts only: names, hashes, owner kind, type code, read-only flag and how each was measured; no documentation text. GSC objects also accept arbitrary script-defined fields: a name absent from this list is not an error by itself.

source.description: Where the facts come from, e.g. "extracted from game executable".

sources.description: Ids from sources.toml behind the file: the extraction, and each oracle or name source used.

hash_family.description: gsc_hash family id of the `hash` field (t7.canon ...).

extraction.description: How the catalogue was produced: tool, executable identity, the registration function, entry layout, per-kind counts and the tables.

class.description: The VM's field class (classnum) the table is registered on.

offset_base.description: High bits the registration ORs into every offset of this table (owner sub-kind within the class).

types.description: Numeric type code of the entries -> label. The label and its agreement count say how the code was named.

kind.description: Owner object kind. entity: every entity; sentient, actor, player, vehicle: entities of that sort (fields valid only on them); hudelem, pathnode, vehiclenode, weapon: other script object classes; centity, dynent: client-VM entities.

vms.description: VMs that register the field: gsc (server), csc (client).

name.description: Lower-case name; present only when a string hashing to `hash` is known.

name_source.description: Where the name string came from; the hash match is the proof.

offset.description: The value the VM stores for the field and hands to the class's getter and setter (offset_base | entry index).

type.description: The entry's numeric type code; see `types`.

read_only.description: true: assigning the field from script raises a read-only error. Absent when not measured.

evidence.description: How the entry was measured: registration, table entry, read-only measure.
